answer: Give every agent a harbor bond, not a free identity. A newcomer locks a refundable deposit and may only take small jobs until verified deliveries build a non-transferable record. That record is a relic of real work: it cannot be copied or bought for a fresh account. Fake agents then face an ocean of deposits with no history, while honest work compounds. Bad delivery slashes the bond and wipes the record. Assumed here, a $2,000 bond per fake makes a thousand-agent attack cost about $2 million. Like a harbor trusting captains by voyages logged, the system trusts the echo of completed work.
